summary:
Round-three machine validation passed with zero errors. Both historical validation reports also passed. Independently matched the Logistics JSON times and volunteer assignments to the Markdown tables. The six activities run in brief order and cover 16:00–19:00 local time continuously: welcome and check-in (16:00–16:25), icebreaker (16:25–16:45), career panel (16:45–17:30), structured networking (17:30–18:15), refreshment break (18:15–18:40), and closing activity (18:40–19:00). The plan uses six volunteers. V4 verifies the step-free route and restroom and staffs access at entry. V1 or acting V3 holds admission pending an accessible route. Accessibility measures include clear aisles, integrated seating, accommodation intake, large-print and plain-text agendas, spoken and written changes, flexible participation, quiet seating, and seated refreshment delivery. For AV or Wi-Fi failure V6 switches to printed and spoken cues. At the 16:35 speaker check V3 reallocates questions or prepares facilitated peer discussion. V1 or acting V3 coordinates volunteer absences. V5 or backup V2 handles shortages, escalating outstanding deficits to V1 or acting V3.

Recalculated the six purchases from the catalog and reconciled quantities and prices against both Markdown supply tables. SNACK10 provides 30 servings (3 × 10) for 4200 cents, FRUIT10 provides 30 (3 × 10) for 3000 cents, WATER24 provides 72 (3 × 24) for 2400 cents, TAG25 provides 75 (3 × 25) for 1350 cents, MARKER4 provides eight (2 × 4) for 700 cents, and PRINT25 provides 75 copies (3 × 25) for 1950 cents. The 60 food servings, 72 drinks, and 75 tags each cover 50 students. Purchases total 13600 cents, the reserve is 16400 cents, and the total reaches the 30000-cent cap. Both plans count the venue, tables, chairs, projector, and Wi-Fi as free and allocate eight shared markers, 50 double-sided large-print attendee agendas with prompts, and 25 copies for signs or backups. Budget calls for confirming the double-sided and mixed-use print assumptions. After usable surplus is applied, round remaining food and drink deficits up separately to whole FRUIT10 and WATER24 packs at 1000 and 800 cents respectively. V1 or acting V3 authorizes timely replenishment. The 13400-cent cumulative draw limit leaves 3000 cents in reserve. The optional one-pack substitution preserves 60 food servings and shifts 400 cents to reserve if adopted after the stated dietary and supply checks.

Each Marketing r3 piece stands alone with Women in Tech: Connect & Grow, Friday, February 19, 2027, 16:00–19:00 local time, room for 50 college students, all six matching activities, and [Venue], [RSVP link], and [Accessibility contact]. The flyer and email use [Speaker names]. Instagram identifies no speakers by name. Participation options and agenda formats match Logistics, and Budget supports the flyer and email offer of one food and one drink per attendee. The three pieces added an unconditional step-free claim in r3 that needs qualification. Logistics still addresses its marketing handoff to r2, whose schedule and participation details carry through to r3. Budget r3 links to current Logistics supply and desk sections. The reverse shortage link still opens Budget r2.

The substantive round-one V5 refreshment fix accepted in round two still holds. Logistics r1's absence row moved V2 to the station during the break, and Budget r1's shortage bullet relied on V5 and V1. The r2 If V5 is absent table and Budget steps 1–4 established the backup, and the r3 counterparts retain V2's count and staging before doors open or at the applicable handoff after a departure. V2 handles food labeling and drink-label checks before release. If V5 leaves during service, V6 pauses the queue while V2 consolidates, reconciles distributed servings against usable stock, stages remaining servings, and checks both labels before clearing the restart. V2 tracks first servings and V4 continues seated delivery. For deficits before or during service, V2 releases usable surplus and recounts, holds seconds, prioritizes outstanding first servings including seated requests, and reports remaining deficits immediately by item to V1 or acting V3. Both label checks also cover replacement stock.

The round-one V1 program fix accepted in round two also holds. Logistics r1 transferred coordination and cues without allocating V1's attendee-facing duties. The r2 and r3 If V1 is absent tables allocate all six blocks. In r3 V3 decides admission after V4's route check, receives speakers, welcomes attendees and cues the icebreaker, while V2 or accepting V6 covers check-in and supplies. V3 leads and wraps the icebreaker with V6 or V2 staging speakers. V3 announces and times the panel while moderating, with V6 handling AV and networking instructions when available. V6 calls networking changes and staggers release. V3 gives the serving and return cues, authorizes replenishment as confirmed by Budget r3 step 3, and leads the closing reflection, sharing, recap, and dismissal. A mid-event handoff starts in the current block and V3 gives imminent cues as needed. One outstanding finding is verified in this round. The stale shortage link and the two additional material gaps prevent approval.

findings.evidence: The Budget handoff in outputs/demo-02/logistics-r2/logistics.md named Budget revision 1. The Budget handoff in outputs/demo-02/logistics-r3/logistics.md now says Budget r2 and its actual link, ../budget-r2/budget.md#refreshment-shortage-procedure, resolves to the existing r2 shortage section. That section covers V2-to-V3 escalation and V3's replenishment authority but only provides the older pre-opening overlap instruction, with no mid-welcome acceptance protocol or speaker transition fallback. The Review note in outputs/demo-02/budget-r3/budget.md identifies the stale link. Budget r3 steps 1–3 agree with Logistics r3 on current desk coverage, V2's immediate item-level report to V3 when both leads are absent, and V3's authority to authorize timely whole-pack replenishment within the reserve limit.
findings.impact: Volunteers following the operational link can miss the accepted desk transfer and speaker fallback during an overlapping absence while handling a shortage.
findings.request: Update the Logistics Budget handoff label and target to ../budget-r3/budget.md#refreshment-shortage-procedure. Preserve the explicit V2-to-V3 escalation and replenishment authority and verify the link opens the r3 procedure with the current opening coverage.

findings.evidence: The accessibility paragraph in each section of outputs/demo-02/marketing-r3/marketing.md says the route from arrival to seating, refreshments, and the restroom is step-free. The venue remains [Venue]. Setup and accessibility in outputs/demo-02/logistics-r3/logistics.md assigns V4 to verify the full route before doors open and arrange a verified alternative if needed. V1 or acting V3 holds admission until an accessible route is available.
findings.impact: Attendees who depend on step-free access can make plans based on a route that still requires confirmation or may change.
findings.request: In all three pieces, describe step-free access as planned and say where verified route information will be shared. Retain [Accessibility contact] for advance questions and reserve a confirmed route claim for after verification.

findings.evidence: In outputs/demo-02/logistics-r3/logistics.md, the welcome staffing row assigns V2 tags and the desk at 16:22, and Setup and accessibility assigns V2 written schedule updates. The volunteer-absence contingency for V2 only folds questions into the panel and switches to one refreshment station. The separate opening-desk handoff applies when V5 is absent.
findings.impact: If V2 is absent, arrivals can lose staffed check-in when V1 starts the welcome, and attendees who rely on written updates may miss schedule changes.
findings.request: Assign an explicit backup for tags, agendas, and desk coverage at 16:22 when V2 is absent. Assign an owner for written schedule updates and specify how the desk backup takes over while V4 continues access coverage.

verified.evidence: In outputs/demo-02/logistics-r2/logistics.md, the combined-absence paragraph covered stock work already underway at opening, while the V5 departure row let V2 step away during welcome without an accepted desk transfer. The Opening desk handoff in outputs/demo-02/logistics-r3/logistics.md and linked step 1 in outputs/demo-02/budget-r3/budget.md cover both absences known before opening with V6 confirming to V3 and staffing first arrivals unless V2 confirms readiness to open. If V1 is already absent when V5 leaves, before or after 16:22 V2 stays until V6 accepts in person. If V5 is absent first, V6 is stationed beside the desk during stock work and takes ownership immediately if V1 leaves before 16:22, or continues if V6 already accepted at 16:22. If V2 has the desk when V1 leaves, V2 stays until V6 accepts. While V1 remains on duty, V1 keeps the desk until V2 or V6 accepts at 16:22. On return after stock work and any immediate deficit report, V2 takes a briefing and explicitly accepts before V6 leaves, or resumes tag support until 16:22 if V1 still owns the desk. The desk owner handles check-in, agendas and tags, V6 gives seat directions from the desk when covering, and V4 stays on access. V3 gives the 16:22 welcome when acting lead. If V6 still owns the desk at 16:38 and V1 is absent, V6 signals V2 and V3 and stays with arrivals. V2 pauses stock work, briefs and stages speakers by 16:42 while V3 wraps the icebreaker, then finishes stock work and accepts the desk. V3 starts the 16:45 panel in discussion format if V6 is still covering arrivals.
